abstract: K\"uhnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.
hook: A 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus cannot exist, narrowing a 15-vertex record.
summary: A known triangulation uses 15 vertices, and it was conjectured minimal. The author rules out 13 vertices by combining a g2 inequality, a reduction to a nine-vertex model, fundamental group analysis and Alexander duality. The 14-vertex case, needed to prove minimality, stays open.
title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
